headlines.title: Early Uber Investor Jason Calacanis Predicts Waymo Could Buy Lucid Or Rivian — Calls Its Chinese-Car Optics ‘Really Bad’
headlines.summary: Calacanis previously disclosed small investments in Lucid, Rivian, WeRide and Pony.ai, predicting takeovers within two years.

headlines.title: Uber Technologies (UBER) Is Generating Cash, but Can Robotaxi Spending Preserve Its Valuation?
headlines.summary: Uber Technologies, Inc. (NYSE:UBER) is approaching a difficult valuation test: its established ride-hailing network is producing more cash, while autonomous vehicles threaten to change who controls transportation demand. On September 2, the Financial Times reported plans to eliminate 3,300 corporate jobs, or about 10% of the global workforce, as the company redirects resources toward robotaxis.

headlines.title: Uber Technologies (UBER) Launches Offsite Advertising Using Its First Party Data
headlines.summary: Uber Technologies (NYSE:UBER) is partnering with TripleLift to extend Uber Advertising audiences beyond Uber's own apps. The new offsite audience expansion product uses Uber's first party mobility and delivery data to target users across the open web. This collaboration marks Uber Advertising's first effort to monetize its data as an external media targeting layer for advertisers.

headlines.title: Uber and Lyft Drivers in California Now Have a Gig Worker Rarity: A Union
headlines.summary: Independent contractors, especially gig workers, aren’t often afforded the same rights as employees. That's changed for Uber and Lyft workers in California.

headlines.title: Will Uber (UBER) Beat Estimates Again in Its Next Earnings Report?
headlines.summary: Uber (UBER) has an impressive earnings surprise history and currently possesses the right combination of the two key ingredients for a likely beat in its next quarterly report.

description: Uber Technologies, Inc. develops and operates proprietary technology applications in the United States, Canada, Latin America, Europe, the Middle East, Africa, and the Asia Pacific. The company operates through three segments: Mobility, Delivery, and Freight. The Mobility segment connects consumers with a range of transportation modalities, such as ridesharing, carsharing, micromobility, rentals, public transit, taxis, and other modalities; and offers riders in a variety of vehicle types, as well as financial partnerships products and advertising services. The Delivery segment allows consumers to search for and discover restaurants to grocery, alcohol, convenience, and other retailers, as well as order a meal or other items, and either pick-up at the restaurant or have it delivered; and provides Uber direct, a white-label delivery-as-a-service for retailers and restaurants, as well as advertising services. The Freight segment manages transportation and logistics networks, which connects shippers and carriers in digital marketplace, including carriers upfronts, pricing, and shipment booking; and offers on-demand platform to automate logistics end-to-end transactions for small-and medium-sized businesses to global enterprises. Uber Technologies, Inc. has strategic partnership with Mews to embed ride booking, real-time tracking and integrated billing directly into the Mews platform. The company was formerly known as Ubercab, Inc. and changed its name to Uber Technologies, Inc. in February 2011. Uber Technologies, Inc. was founded in 2009 and is headquartered in San Francisco, California.
